title: QwenLM/qwen-code: a terminal coding agent you can point at more than one provider
friendlyTitle: Qwen Code is a terminal coding agent that can use more than one model provider
summary: Qwen Code was on GitHub Trending today with 151 stars in the day and about 29,700 overall. It is an open-source terminal coding agent, with desktop, editor, web, and chat clients. The license is Apache 2.0. It can use Qwen, OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, or a local server such as Ollama or vLLM. Node 22 or newer is required for the npm install. A Qwen Plus or Pro subscription, or an API key, is required to sign in.
friendlySummary: Qwen Code was trending on GitHub today, with 151 new stars and about 29,700 in total. It is an open-source coding agent for the terminal, and it also has desktop, editor, web, and chat apps. The license is Apache 2.0. It can use Qwen, OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, or a local model server. You need Node 22 or newer for the npm install, and a subscription or an API key to sign in.
whyItMatters: Run qwen in a project when you want one agent harness and the freedom to change the model behind it. There is also a desktop app, and qwen serve for a local web view. That server listens on your machine without a token by default. On a shared computer, set QWEN_SERVER_TOKEN and require auth. Their SWE-bench Verified scores, 76.4 to 77.8 percent, used Qwen 3.7 Max and are their own measurement.
